Oak Data Research Questions:

Differences in germination rates between acorns between treatments?

Are there differences in seedling growth rates between treatments (microhabitats)

Which Microclimates had teh highest rate of natural recruits

In which microclimates were the plants healthiest (e.g., highest leaf greeness)

Oak Exploratory Data Analysis and Cleaning

For each question;

Which data can we use?

```{r}
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)
#This code was gotten by clicking the files on the right and clicking import, the input can be edited and the code is generated for coping and pasting. 
library(readxl)
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean <- read_excel("Oak Project/Data/Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7&6Clean.xlsx", 
    sheet = "Input1", skip = 1)
View(Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean)
names(Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean)
```

```{r}
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean <-
  Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean %>% #assigned by use of <- but also needed to CALL it in order for R to understand where to rename. 
 dplyr:: rename( Page_Num ="Page #", 
          Date = "MM/DD/YYYY",
          Recorder ="Name",
         Block ="#...4",
         Tag_Num ="#...5",
         Oak_Type ="NR, S, or A",
         Treatment ="AC, OA, NP, DT, or DL",
         OA_microclimate ="TH, TI, CN",
         Seedling_Ht_Cm ="(cm)",
         Num_Leaves ="#...10",
         Num_Dead_Leaves ="#...11",
         Leaf_Greenness ="%",
         Num_Germinated ="#...13",
         RCD ="(mm)",
        Notes  ="as written on data sheet")
Survival_HeightApril26Blocks7_6Clean
```

Things about this data that need to be cleaned up; Conversion of VALUES to NA & Split Tag \#

Column Separation,

We need rows for each planted acorn that did not germinate, this would create more NAs but summaries would make much more sense.

To import and merge spreadsheets;

```{r}
install.packages("plyr") #contains the lapply function
library("dplyr")
library("plyr")
library("readr")
library("readxl")

```

```{r}
oak_data <- list.files(path = "Oak Project/Data",
                       pattern = "*6Clean.xlsx",
                       full.names = TRUE) |> #asking all files that have a pattern, we are excluding OCT2025
  lapply(read_excel,
         na = "NA", sheet = "Input1", skip = 1) |> 
  bind_rows()
#Takes four seperate data sheets and staples them together in one datasheet, lines columns together
#takes the excel sheet and applies it to all files 
names(oak_data)
unloadNamespace("plyr")
```

```{r}
oak_data <-
  oak_data |> 
dplyr:: rename(Page_Num ="Page #", 
                       Date = "MM/DD/YYYY",
                       Recorder ="Name",
                       Block ="#...4",
                       Tag_Num ="#...5",
                       Oak_Type ="NR, S, or A",
                       Treatment ="AC, OA, NP, DT, or DL",
                       OA_microclimate ="TH, TI, CN",
                       Seedling_Ht_Cm ="(cm)",
                       Num_Leaves ="#...10",
                       Num_Dead_Leaves ="#...11",
                       Leaf_Greenness ="%",
                       Num_Germinated ="#...13",
                       RCD ="(mm)",
                       Notes  ="as written on data sheet")

oak_data
```

```{r}
view(oak_data)
```

```{r}
oak_data_CLEAN <- oak_data |> 
  separate ('Tag_Num', into = c("Tag_Num", "Acorn_Num"), sep = "A") |> 
  mutate(Tag_Num = as.numeric(Tag_Num)) |> 
  mutate(Acorn_Num = as.numeric(Acorn_Num)) |> 
  
  mutate(Leaf_Greenness = as.numeric(Leaf_Greenness),
         Dead = case_when(
           Seedling_Ht_Cm == 0 ~ "Dead",
           Seedling_Ht_Cm > 0 ~ "Alive"
         )) ##VALUES TO NA, case when = if then  
#
oak_data_CLEAN
#Breaks up the original tag number oclumn into tag number and acorn nuber by seperating by A. 
#mutate makes new columns, can change exisiting columns
#This good, continue cleaning from this
# ' = if column name has a space between, it keeps the words together 
```

```{r}
oak_data_CLEAN |> 
  select(Tag_Num, Acorn_Num) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  arrange(Tag_Num)

Acorn_ID_Table <- oak_data_CLEAN |> 
  select(Tag_Num, Block, Treatment, OA_microclimate, Date) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  arrange(Tag_Num) |> 
  mutate(Acorn1 = 1, Acorn2 = 2, Acorn3 = 3) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols  = c(Acorn1, Acorn2, Acorn3),
    names_to = "whatever",
    values_to = "Acorn_Num") |> 
  select(-whatever)
view(oak_data_CLEAN)
```

```{r}
Acorn_ID_Table
full_join(Acorn_ID_Table) #Full join looks for matching columns and then combines matching column. 

#This is all a mess, ignore
```
